entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Properzia de' Rossi was an Italian Renaissance sculptor who, in 1533, became one of only four women to receive a biography in Vasari's Lives of the Artists, marking a significant milestone in the recognition of female artists during the Renaissance.

Born in Mantua, Italy, de' Rossi's artistic talent and innovative style were shaped by her training under the renowned artist Jacopo da Bologna.

Her most notable works include the bronze sculpture 'Madonna and Child' (1531) and 'St. Sebastian' (1533), which showcased her mastery of classical techniques and emotional depth.

De' Rossi's artistic legacy extends beyond her individual works, as she paved the way for future generations of female artists, including the likes of Sofonisba Anguissola and Artemisia Gentileschi.

In the annals of art history, de' Rossi's name stands as a testament to the enduring power of female creativity and artistic expression during the Renaissance.
